Let $\omega_0$ be a finite signed Borel measure on $\mathbb R^2$, set $M=|\omega_0|(\mathbb R^2)$, and let $\omega_0=\omega_0^+-\omega_0^-$ be its Jordan decomposition. $$Z_t(x,s)=x+M\int_0^t\int_E rK_\varepsilon(Z_u(x,s)-Z_u(y,r))\,d\lambda_0(y,r)\,du,$$

such that its time-supremum function is measurable and $\int_E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|Z_t(x,s)|\,d\lambda_0(x,s)<\infty$. It represents the signed measure curve

$$\omega_t=M\int_E s\,\delta_{Z_t(x,s)}\,d\lambda_0(x,s).$$

def-gauss-moment-data: Definition gives the displayed definition/formula rather than asserting an equivalence between independently stated propositions. No separate necessity implication is asserted by its formula. Exact current Definition anchor: Let $a<b$ be real numbers, let $m\ge1$ be an integer, and let
$r\in\{2m-1,2m\}$. A **Gaussian quadrature moment datum of order $r$** is a
finite positive measure $\mu$ on the relative Borel sigma-algebra
$\mathcal B([a,b])$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]], [[def-measure-space]],
[[def-measure]], [[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]) such that
$\mu([a,b])>0$, and whose **relative support**
$$ S_\mu:=\{x\in[a,b]:\mu(U)>0\text{ for every relatively open }U\subseteq[a,b]\text{ with }x\in U\} $$
contains at least $m+1$ distinct points. For every integer $0\le k\le r$,
require $x\mapsto |x|^k$ to be integrable with respect to $\mu$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]) and put
$M_k:=\int_{[a,b]}x^k\,d\mu(x)$. Powers use the natural-exponent
recursion of [[def-integer-power]], with $x^0=1$ for every real $x$, including
$x=0$; thus $M_0$ is the integral of the constant function $1$.

The branch $r=2m-1$ supplies all moments used to construct the monic
degree-$m$ orthogonal polynomial and prove rule exactness. The stronger branch
$r=2m$ also defines its squared norm and is used for the remainder formula.
Because $[a,b]$ is bounded and $\mu$ is finite, these absolute-moment
integrability conditions follow from finiteness; they are stated to make the
two moment interfaces explicit.

does not verify them. All interval operations use
[[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]]. Any overflow, invalid
domain, nonpositive divisor, failed solve, undecidable comparison, or failed
certification returns `inconclusive`.

right-hand side
$$ (H_k)_{ij}=\mu_{i+j},\qquad (b_k)_i=-\mu_{i+k} \quad(0\le i,j<k) $$
by the corresponding moment intervals. Take the exact rational midpoints of
these interval data and use exact Gaussian elimination with row swaps to the
first available nonzero pivot to produce point proposals for $H_k^{-1}$ and
$-H_k^{-1}b_k$. If a pivot is zero, return `inconclusive`. Round every
proposal down to a finite dyadic in the selected format; on overflow, return
`inconclusive`. Call
[[alg-uniform-interval-linear-residual-certifier]] on the full rectangle

coefficient of the unique solution by its reported center plus or minus the
outward-rounded uniform error radius. These intervals enclose the coefficients
of $p_k(X)=X^k+\sum_{j<k}c_{kj}X^j$ whenever the moment promise holds.

$$ h_j=\sum_{r,s=0}^{j}c_{jr}c_{js}\mu_{r+s},\qquad \alpha_j=\frac{\sum_{r,s=0}^{j}c_{jr}c_{js}\mu_{r+s+1}}{h_j}, $$

positive lower endpoint, or a division or square root is not certified on its
domain, return `inconclusive`. Form a real symmetric interval Jacobi matrix
$\mathcal J$ with diagonal intervals $\alpha_j$ and mirrored off-diagonal
intervals $\sqrt{\beta_j}$; reuse the same interval in each mirrored pair.

with those diagonal and mirrored off-diagonal entries and all other entries

contains the true Jacobi matrix.

count $m-1$, restart budget $N_{\max}=1$, thick restart mode, and zero

finite positive measure $\mu$ on the relative Borel sigma-algebra
$\mathcal B([a,b])$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]], [[def-measure-space]],
[[def-measure]], [[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]) such that
$\mu([a,b])>0$, and whose **relative support**
$$ S_\mu:=\{x\in[a,b]:\mu(U)>0\text{ for every relatively open }U\subseteq[a,b]\text{ with }x\in U\} $$
contains at least $m+1$ distinct points. For every integer $0\le k\le r$,
require $x\mapsto |x|^k$ to be integrable with respect to $\mu$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]) and put
$M_k:=\int_{[a,b]}x^k\,d\mu(x)$. Powers use the natural-exponent
recursion of [[def-integer-power]], with $x^0=1$ for every real $x$, including
$x=0$; thus $M_0$ is the integral of the constant function $1$.

degree-$m$ orthogonal polynomial and prove rule exactness. The stronger branch
$r=2m$ also defines its squared norm and is used for the remainder formula.

integrability conditions follow from finiteness; they are stated to make the
two moment interfaces explicit.

def-gauss-moment-data: m=1 needs at least two support points; m=0 and zero measure are excluded. The k=0 moment is M0=mass and x^0=1 even at x=0. Exact current Definition anchor: Let $a<b$ be real numbers, let $m\ge1$ be an integer, and let
$r\in\{2m-1,2m\}$. A **Gaussian quadrature moment datum of order $r$** is a
finite positive measure $\mu$ on the relative Borel sigma-algebra
$\mathcal B([a,b])$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]], [[def-measure-space]],
[[def-measure]], [[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]) such that
$\mu([a,b])>0$, and whose **relative support**
$$ S_\mu:=\{x\in[a,b]:\mu(U)>0\text{ for every relatively open }U\subseteq[a,b]\text{ with }x\in U\} $$
contains at least $m+1$ distinct points. For every integer $0\le k\le r$,
require $x\mapsto |x|^k$ to be integrable with respect to $\mu$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]) and put
$M_k:=\int_{[a,b]}x^k\,d\mu(x)$. Powers use the natural-exponent
recursion of [[def-integer-power]], with $x^0=1$ for every real $x$, including
$x=0$; thus $M_0$ is the integral of the constant function $1$.

degree-$m$ orthogonal polynomial and prove rule exactness. The stronger branch
$r=2m$ also defines its squared norm and is used for the remainder formula.
Because $[a,b]$ is bounded and $\mu$ is finite, these absolute-moment
integrability conditions follow from finiteness; they are stated to make the
two moment interfaces explicit.

thm-hermite-interpolant-double-node-remainder: Only the finite construction or individual existential witness in the displayed result is used here; no simultaneous arbitrary-family selection is asserted. For m=1 the cardinal polynomial is1 and H is the tangent affine interpolant. Zero f or f derivative is allowed; at a node both error and product vanish, without division by zero. Exact current Statement anchor: Let $m\ge1$, let $a<b$, let $x_1<\cdots<x_m$ lie in $(a,b)$, and let
$f\in C^{2m}([a,b],\mathbb R)$. Let $\ell_i$ be the Lagrange cardinal
polynomials for these nodes as in
[[def-cardinal-polynomial-interpolation]]. Define
$$ H(t):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\left[f(x_i)\bigl(1-2\ell_i'(x_i)(t-x_i)\bigr)+f'(x_i)(t-x_i)\right]\ell_i(t)^2. $$

$H'(x_i)=f'(x_i)$ for every $i$. If $x\in[a,b]$ is not a node, there is

$$ f(x)-H(x)=\frac{f^{(2m)}(\xi_x)}{(2m)!_{\mathbb R}}\prod_{i=1}^{m}(x-x_i)^2, $$
where $(2m)!_{\mathbb R}:=\prod_{j=1}^{2m}j$.

so it gives order-three moment data for $m=2$. The moments are
$\mu_0=2$, $\mu_1=0$, $\mu_2=2/3$, and $\mu_3=0$. The monic orthogonal
polynomials through degree two are $p_0=1$, $p_1=X$, and
$p_2=X^2-1/3$. Thus the Gaussian nodes are

$$ J_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&1/\sqrt3\\1/\sqrt3&0\end{pmatrix}. $$

$j=0,\ldots,m$ there is a unique monic real polynomial $p_j$ of degree $j$
such that
$$ \int_{[a,b]}p_j(x)q(x)\,d\mu(x)=0 $$

$(q_0(x_i),\ldots,q_{m-1}(x_i))^{\mathsf T}$ is a nonzero eigenvector of $J_m$

after.evidence:
def-stiefel-grassmann-optimization-conventions: For r=1 frames are unit vectors; r=n gives the full orthogonal group and the one-point full-dimensional Grassmann quotient. The matrix X=0 is excluded by X^T X=I, while zero tangent vectors are included in the horizontal subspace. Exact current Definition anchor: For integers $1\le r\le n$, the **real Stiefel manifold** is
$$\operatorname{St}(n,r):=\{X\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}:X^{\mathsf T}X=I_r\}.$$
The **real Grassmannian** $\operatorname{Gr}(r,n)$ is the set of $r$-dimensional
linear subspaces of $\mathbb R^n$, identified with the quotient of
$\operatorname{St}(n,r)$ by the right action $X\mapsto XQ$ of
$\operatorname O(r)$. A frame $X$ represents the subspace
$[X]=\operatorname{range}(X)$.

On matrix spaces use the Frobenius inner product
$\langle U,V\rangle_F=\operatorname{tr}(U^{\mathsf T}V)$. Give Stiefel its
induced metric. On the Grassmann quotient use the quotient metric: identify a
tangent vector at $[X]$ with its unique horizontal representative $Z$ satisfying
$X^{\mathsf T}Z=0$, and pair horizontal representatives by the Frobenius inner
product. A Grassmann formula written with a frame representative must be
unchanged under $(X,Z)\mapsto(XQ,ZQ)$ for $Q\in\operatorname O(r)$.

For a matrix $M$, set $\operatorname{sym}(M)=(M+M^{\mathsf T})/2$.

def-complex-grassmann-polar-retraction: At eta=0, I+eta*eta=I and the output is X. At r=n the horizontal equation X*eta=0 forces eta=0. Hermitian square root. The horizontal condition gives
$(X+\eta)^*(X+\eta)=I+\eta^*\eta\succ0$, so this map is defined for every
horizontal tangent vector, and its frame representative is unchanged as a
Grassmann point when $(X,\eta)$ is replaced by $(XQ,\eta Q)$ with unitary $Q$.

def-stiefel-qr-polar-retractions: At eta=0 the positive-diagonal QR is X I and the polar Gram factor is I. For every tangent eta, ||(X+eta)v||^2=||v||^2+||eta v||^2 proves full rank even at r=n; the positive norms in the finite Gram-Schmidt recursion never vanish. Exact current Definition anchor: For $X\in\operatorname{St}(n,r)$ and $\eta\in T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)$,
put $Y=X+\eta$. On the domain where $Y$ has full column rank, let
$\operatorname{qf}(Y)$ be the $Q$ factor in the unique reduced QR factorization
$Y=QR$ with $R$ upper triangular and positive diagonal. Define the **QR map**
by $R_X^{\rm QR}(\eta)=\operatorname{qf}(X+\eta)$. Define the **polar map**
by
$$R_X^{\rm pol}(\eta)=(X+\eta)\bigl((X+\eta)^{\mathsf T}(X+\eta)\bigr)^{-1/2},$$
where the exponent denotes the inverse of the unique positive-definite square
root. Both Stiefel maps induce Grassmann maps by taking the output column space.
The polar formula is right-equivariant:
$R_{XQ}^{\rm pol}(\eta Q)=R_X^{\rm pol}(\eta)Q$ for every $Q\in\operatorname O(r)$.

These are defined only where the displayed input is full rank. In fact, for a
Stiefel tangent $\eta$, $X+\eta$ always has full column rank, since
$\|(X+\eta)v\|_2^2=\|v\|_2^2+\|\eta v\|_2^2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^r$.

be smooth, and choose one retraction $R$ from

Fix $a\in(0,1)$, $\beta\in(0,1)$ and an integer budget $J\ge0$.

$t_j=\beta^j$ for $j=0,\ldots,J$. At each trial form $y_j=R_x(-t_jg)$;

with
$$f(y_j)\le f(x)-a t_j\|g\|^2.$$
If no trial passes, return `(x, budget-exhausted)`.

def-stiefel-grassmann-projected-vector-transport: The displayed maps send Z=0 to0. At eta=0 the endpoint is X and tangency/horizontality cancels the projection correction, returning Z. At r=n the Grassmann horizontal space is{0}; the real Stiefel tangent need not be zero. Exact current Definition anchor: Let $X$ be a source frame, $\eta\in T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)$, and
$Z\in T_X\operatorname{St}(n,r)$. For Stiefel transport let $Y=R_X(\eta)$ be
either the QR or polar endpoint. For Grassmann transport specifically choose
$Y=R_X^{\rm pol}(\eta)$, the polar endpoint; the positive-diagonal QR frame is
not used for this representative-based quotient transport. Define the
**projected Stiefel transport**
$$\mathcal T_Y^{\rm St}(Z):=Z-Y\operatorname{sym}(Y^{\mathsf T}Z),$$
and, for a horizontal source representative $Z$, define the **projected Grassmann transport representative**
$$\mathcal T_Y^{\rm Gr}(Z):=(I-YY^{\mathsf T})Z.$$
The Grassmann expression is interpreted as a tangent representative at
$[Y]$. The polar endpoint is right-equivariant, so the next proposition verifies
representative independence, tangency, and identity at a zero step. These
projection transports are not claimed to be Levi-Civita parallel transport.

The reciprocal convention includes this degenerate bound; Proof3.1 includes j=0,t=1, and threshold equality t=delta is admitted. Exact current Statement anchor: Let $M=\operatorname{St}(n,r)$ or $\operatorname{Gr}(r,n)$ be compact, let
$f:M\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, and let $R$ be a QR or polar retraction with the
first-order property of [[thm-stiefel-retractions-are-first-order]]. Write
$\widehat f_x(\eta)=f(R_x(\eta))$. Assume a uniform bound
$\|\operatorname{grad}f(x)\|\le G$ and a constant $L_R\ge0$ such that, for
every $x$ and $\|\eta\|\le1$,
$$\|\operatorname{grad}\widehat f_x(\eta)-\operatorname{grad}\widehat f_x(0)\|\le L_R\|\eta\|.$$
For $a\in(0,1)$ and a nonstationary iterate, set
$$\delta=\min\{1,(2G)^{-1},2(1-a)/L_R\},$$

backtracking budget tests some $t_j=\beta^j\le\delta$, then it accepts a step;
the first accepted step obeys $t\ge\beta\delta$. The bound
$t\|\operatorname{grad}f(x)\|\le1/2$ keeps the pullback argument inside its
assumed unit tangent ball.

Let $\omega_t$ be a smooth finite signed vorticity density on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^2$ with finite first moment, transported by a sign-preserving characteristic flow $X_t$ satisfying $\omega_t=(X_t)_\#\omega_0$ and $\dot X_t(x)=(K*\omega_t)(X_t(x))$, where $K$ is the singular kernel in [[def-mollified-biot-savart-vortex-kernel]]. Assume $\sup_{t\le T}\|\omega_t\|_\infty\le W$, $\int\sup_{t\le T}|X_t(x)|d|\omega_0|(x)<\infty$, and the flow transports each Jordan part to the corresponding Jordan part. Put $M=|\omega_0|(\mathbb R^2)$. Let
$$\omega_N^0=\sum_{i=1}^N\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i^0}$$
be a finite signed particle measure whose positive and negative Jordan masses respectively equal those of $\omega_0$, with finite first moment, and with consolidated atoms whose positive and negative supports are disjoint; thus $\sum_i|\Gamma_i|=M$. Let $E_0=C_{\pm}(\omega_0,\omega_N^0)<\infty$.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$. For every time and force location $(t,x)$, suppose the force integrand $F_{t,x}:R\to\mathbb R^2$ lies in $C^4(R,\mathbb R^2)$ and its fourth partial derivatives satisfy the uniform bounds $M_{40},M_{04}$. Let the tensor Simpson evaluator use the even panel counts and widths in [[thm-tensor-simpson-force-error]], and define its residual by $r_q(t,x)=Q_yQ_xF_{t,x}-\int_R F_{t,x}$. Thus
$$\eta_q=\frac{\sqrt2|R|}{180}(h_x^4M_{40}+h_y^4M_{04}).$$
Assume this residual is the same correction function for every particle, $\sup_{t,x}|r_q(t,x)|\le\eta_q$, and the corrected regularized particle flow preserves the two Jordan parts. Write $x_i^{\varepsilon,q}$ for the exact solution from $x_i^0$ of
$$\dot x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)=\sum_{j=1}^N\Gamma_jK_\varepsilon(x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)-x_j^{\varepsilon,q}(t))+r_q(t,x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)),$$
and set $\omega_N^{\varepsilon,q}(t)=\sum_i\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i^{\varepsilon,q}(t)}$. Assume $r_q$ and the resulting finite-dimensional particle field are jointly $C^4$ in time and state with derivatives through order four bounded on a compact tube containing all exact paths and RK4 stages. Let $x_i^h(T)$ be the RK4 states from the same initial data for this ODE, and define $\omega_{N,h}^{\varepsilon,q}(T)=\sum_i\Gamma_i\delta_{x_i^h(T)}$. Let $h=T/n\le h_0$ for an integer $n\ge1$ and define $C_{RK}:=C_4(e^{L_*T}-1)/L_*$ if $L_*>0$, and $C_{RK}:=C_4T$ if $L_*=0$, where $C_4,L_*,h_0$ are the constants in [[thm-rk4-global-error-for-regularized-vortex-particles]]. Then
$$d_{BL}(\omega_T,\omega_{N,h}^{\varepsilon,q}(T)) \le e^{2L_\varepsilon MT}\left(E_0+MT\left(C_\rho\varepsilon W+\eta_q\right)\right)+MC_{RK}h^4,$$
where $L_\varepsilon$ is a one-variable global Lipschitz constant for $K_\varepsilon$; the induced two-variable constant for $K_\varepsilon(x-y)$ is also $L_\varepsilon$. The terms are initial signed particle approximation, blob regularization, force quadrature, and RK4 time error. The constants may depend on $\varepsilon$, particle count, and the tube; no uniform singular limit as $\varepsilon\to0$ is claimed.

The RK4 tube condition in the Statement includes all numerical grid states and every stage generated at each grid step from both the exact solution start and the numerical start; both one-step maps are defined.

ex-dimension-dependent-empirical-w1-error: N>=1 is required by empirical normalization. For one sample the bound is1-2^-M; when N>=2^M the displayed lower bound may be0 or negative and remains valid, without claiming a negative distance. Exact current Example anchor: Let $V_M=\{0,1\}^M\subset\mathbb R^M$ and let $\mu_M$ be uniform on its $2^M$ vertices. For any empirical measure $\nu_N=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N\delta_{Y_j}$ obtained from $N$ samples $Y_j\in V_M$, the 1-Wasserstein error has the deterministic lower bound
$$W_1(\mu_M,\nu_N)\ge1-\frac{N}{2^M}.$$
Thus no dimension-free bound $W_1(\mu,\mu_N)\le C N^{-1/2}$ can hold uniformly over all dimensions and all empirical samples.

Exact current Example anchor: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\omega_0\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ be nonnegative with mass one, and suppose the smooth Euler flow satisfies $\omega_t=(X_t)_\#\omega_0$, $\dot X_t=(K*\omega_t)(X_t)$, and $\sup_{t\le T}\|\omega_t\|_\infty\le W$, with $\int\sup_{t\le T}|X_t(x)|d\omega_0(x)<\infty$. Approximate it by $N\ge1$ distinct initial positions $x_1^0,\ldots,x_N^0$ with equal weights $1/N$, define $\mu_N^0=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i^0}$, and let $E_0=W_1(\omega_0,\mu_N^0)$. For an integer $n\ge1$ with $h=T/n\le h_0$, let $x_i^h(T)$ be their RK4 approximations from the same initial nodes, with all paths and stages in that tube. Define $\omega_{N,h}^{\varepsilon,q}(T)=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{x_i^h(T)}$. If $C_{RK}$ is the coefficient from [[thm-rk4-global-error-for-regularized-vortex-particles]] for this $h_0$, then

$$W_1(\omega_T,\omega_{N,h}^{\varepsilon,q}(T))\le e^{2L_\varepsilon T}\left(E_0+T(C_\rho\varepsilon W+\eta_q)\right)+C_{RK}h^4.$$

The RK4 tube hypothesis includes all numerical grid states and every stage generated at each grid step from both the exact start and the numerical start, and both one-step maps are defined, as required by [[thm-rk4-global-error-for-regularized-vortex-particles]].
